title: Linear Predictive Coding — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Linear Predictive Coding's rich face: the page's one equation walked up from a sine to a voice, the mirror-twin laid beside Tract Mirror's walk that tests it, and the soul made audible, one spoken sentence driven by its own leftover, a pulse train and a codebook through the same filter. I hold the fingerprint of the words each piece was made against; I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

sections.heading: The autoregressive model and the residual

pieces.file: Linear Predictive Coding — rich — how much is left over.html
pieces.title: how much is left over
pieces.caption: **The compression sentence, measured.** Three steps: a sine predicted from its last sample (one weight leaves sin² ω of it, two leave rounding error); then Wold's split, two sines that four weights take 47 dB out of, noise that no order touches, and a sine in noise whose gain climbs toward the noise's own 17 dB and stops; and last the page's sentence spoken, with the order raised from 1 to 32. The leftover falls 10.1 dB under the voice at one weight and 19.1 dB at eighteen, about 3.2 bits a sample, a fifth of 256 kbps of 16-bit audio, and the next fourteen weights buy 0.4 dB more. The voice is Kokoro, open weights, carried inside the piece; the checks beside it re-run every number.

verdicts.file: Linear Predictive Coding — rich — how much is left over.html
verdicts.why: A test that walks up from one sine to the voice; recomputed with an independent Levinson-Durbin: G(1) 10.13, G(18) 19.05, G(32) 19.49 dB, +0.44 after 18, exactly as printed. Note: name the 256 kbps the 50.6 kbps is out of, and point to the swap piece for where the rest of the compression comes from.

sections.heading: The source-filter model and its mirror-twin

pieces.file: /Projects/Tract Mirror/Tract Mirror — rich — junction to mirror.html
pieces.by: Tract Mirror's rich face, proposal round 2026-11
pieces.title: one joint, then the whole mirror · from Tract Mirror
pieces.caption: **This section's claim, tested in the project that builds it.** Tract Mirror's walk goes from one joint between two tubes up to a vowel, then runs the mirror backward: linear prediction reads the tube out of its own click. The reflection coefficients come back equal to the tube's area-ratio mismatches, joint for joint, only in the ideal tube, with the glottis closed and the walls lossless (largest gap under 10⁻¹¹ on six vowels). With the plugin's leaky glottis and lossy walls they come back as a different tube with the same sound once one level is matched, up to 0.61 off on /o/. Either condition alone breaks the identity. Gathered as it stands, still a proposal on its own page; the finding waits here as an offer.

verdicts.file: /Projects/Tract Mirror/Tract Mirror — rich — junction to mirror.html
verdicts.why: Tests the lattice-equals-mismatch claim and finds its conditions; walks up from one joint. Caption and offer state the finding in the same terms and numbers as Tract Mirror's landed face; the two conform warnings are its sandboxed fetch, with an in-piece fallback it names.

sections.heading: The residual is where the soul hides

pieces.file: Linear Predictive Coding — rich — the residual swap.html
pieces.by: Levinson-Durbin · LPC-10 and CELP, their moves · Kokoro (af_heart) for the voice
pieces.title: keep the filter, change what drives it
pieces.caption: **The soul made audible, walked up.** A made vowel and its formants; ten weights reading them back to within 16 Hz and leaving the buzz (99.5 % of the leftover on the buzz's instants). Then the page's sentence said by Kokoro, a speech model trained on human recordings, so the life measured was itself predicted by a model: its leftover puts only 49.5 % on the beat. The same ten weights, driven by its own leftover, give the voice back to 10⁻¹⁵, by construction, as any weights would. Driven by LPC-10's pulse train (98.2 % on the beat) they keep every formant and lose the waveform (−2.8 dB). Last, a CELP-style codebook brings the waveform back to 8.8 dB for about 3.5 kbps more, matching the leftover as its weighting hears it (0.87), not sample by sample (0.43). All at 8 kHz; no agent has heard the mix.
pieces.near: brought the body back by shipping

verdicts.file: Linear Predictive Coding — rich — the residual swap.html
verdicts.why: A real test (made vowel 99.5 % on the beat, the voice 49.5 %) that walks up, but three wordings outrun it: 'a real voice' (it is Kokoro); 'without copying the leftover' / 'not by how close it sits to the leftover' (the search target is the leftover through 1/A(z/0.8), where the match is 0.87); 'that half, off the beat, is what the page calls the soul' (jitter and shimmer are on the beat). Fix those in the subtitle, step 4 and 5 texts and the caption; optionally say the own-leftover identity cannot fail.

offers.section: The source-filter model and its mirror-twin
offers.what: The page says the lattice's reflection coefficients are the impedance mismatches between the tube's segments. Tract Mirror's walk (gathered beside the sentence) runs LPC (Levinson-Durbin, order 44) on a tube's own click and finds that true only for the ideal tube: glottis closed and walls lossless, where every joint comes back within 10⁻¹¹. With the plugin's leaky glottis (+0.97) and lossy walls (0.996 a joint) the coefficients come back as a different tube with the same sound once one level is matched: gaps 0.25 on /a/, 0.61 on /o/, and either condition alone breaks it. Offer: name both conditions, and that the reading is of the tube's impulse response, where the page says 'they are the impedance mismatches'. The same finding waits as an open offer on Tract Mirror's opening section.

offers.section: The residual is where the soul hides
offers.what: 'The residual sounded like a buzzer because LPC-10 threw the residual away' reads as if the residual were the buzzer. It was the voice: the leftover is the least buzz-like signal in the piece. Energy on the beat: residual 49.5 % on the maker's tracker, 42.2 % on the challenger's; pulse train 98.2 % and 99.7 %; white noise 17 % (challenger). Offer: 'The voice sounded like a buzzer because LPC-10 threw the residual away and replaced it with a pulse train.'

offers.section: The residual is where the soul hides
offers.what: 'A small codebook of excitations — quantized residuals' is the common shorthand and holds where CELP looks: through the weighting 1/A(z/0.8), the piece's chosen excitation matches the residual at 0.87, though sample by sample only 0.43 (challenger 0.45), and it brings the waveform back to 8.8 dB against the pulse train's −2.8 (challenger 8.7 and −3.2). What the phrase leaves out is the method. Offer: keep the word and add it: 'a small codebook of excitations — quantized residuals, each chosen by synthesizing the voice it would make and keeping the closest'.

offers.section: The residual is where the soul hides
offers.what: Only the word 'standard' is early. LPC-10 at 2,400 bps was the secure-voice coder in service in the late 1970s (NSA's STU-I, 1977–79), but the standard dates from 1984 (NATO STANAG 4198, February 1984; FED-STD-1015, 28 November 1984; later FIPS 137). Offer: 'the 2,400 bps secure-voice coder of the late 1970s, a federal standard by 1984'. Checked on the web, not by a piece (Wikipedia's FIPS 137 and LPC-10 articles; the Crypto Museum's LPC-10 and STU-I pages). The swap piece's step-4 note already says 'the 1984 standard', which is accurate.
